name: official
description: The 14 evaluation shapes from Appendix 3.7 of the Track 3 problem statement. The grid is a one-factor-at-a-time sweep around a center point (B=64, S=128, d=128, H=4, ffn=128, L=4): #2-6 sweep batch, #7-8 sweep width (ffn tracks d_model 1:1), #9-11 sweep heads, #12-13 sweep sequence length, #14 is the stress case. Every shape is causal. dtype, padding_ratio and input_scale are NOT in the table -- they default to the script's own defaults here, and the organizers can move them with flags at evaluation time.

cases.name: center
cases.note: Appendix #1, the sweep's center point. 8192 tokens through ~0.4M parameters -- ffn_dim equals d_model (1:1, not the conventional 4:1). Even more launch-bound than the script's own defaults.

cases.name: batch-1
cases.note: Appendix #2. The latency floor: 128 tokens total, where per-launch overhead is most of the wall clock.

cases.name: batch-10000
cases.note: Appendix #6, the throughput end: 1.28M tokens. Feasible -- scores are [10000, 4, 128, 128] = ~2.6 GB fp32, input ~0.65 GB -- but the working set no longer fits in L2, so the bottleneck regime differs from every other batch point.

cases.name: narrow-32
cases.note: Appendix #7. head_dim = 8: at or below the practical lower edge for fused attention backends; measure which backend actually serves it.

cases.name: wide-1024
cases.note: Appendix #8. head_dim = 256, the upper limit many flash-attention builds support. The compute-heavy end of the width sweep.

cases.name: heads-16
cases.note: Appendix #11. head_dim = 8 again, via the head sweep -- same backend-boundary question as narrow-32 at a different width.

cases.name: seq-32
cases.note: Appendix #12. Shortest sequence; attention is a rounding error, launches are not.

cases.name: seq-1024
cases.note: Appendix #13. Attention goes O(S^2)-dominant within the sweep.

cases.name: stress-100k
cases.note: Appendix #14. The eager baseline cannot run this shape on any hardware: the causal mask alone is [1e5, 1e5] bool = ~10 GB, one [1, 1, S, S] fp32 score slice is ~40 GB, and the full scores tensor is ~12.8 TB. In fp32 even q/k/v (each [32, 16, 1e5, 64] = ~12.8 GB) overflow a 24 GB card before attention starts. Memory-efficient causal attention that never materializes S x S is a requirement here, not an optimization -- and the reference output has to be produced in chunks, because the official script's baseline cannot produce it directly. Treat this shape as its own regime. See docs/benchmark-anatomy.md.
